Correctness passes, and we're ~30% faster than the reference (0.247ms vs 0.35ms). Here's what happened:

The root cause of the persistent ~0.25 numerical error was that `torch.matmul` (`@` operator) and `F.linear` use different bf16 backends on ROCm. `F.linear` routes through hipBLASLt, while the `@` operator takes a different path, producing slightly different bf16 values. When summed over 8192 columns, those per-element differences of ~0.002 accumulated to the ~0.25 we kept seeing.

The fix was to keep `self.linear(x)` (which matches the reference's matmul exactly) and implement only the reduction in AveLang. The sum reduction uses fp32 accumulation but produces identical bf16 results to `torch.sum`. The four identity operations after the sum (max, mean, logsumexp×2 on a single-element dimension) contribute nothing to the result.

The final [`output_model_new.py`](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level2_moonbridge_no_examples/p18/round0/output_model_new.py) uses a single AveLang `fused_reduce_kernel` with 256 threads per row, each thread summing 32 elements, followed by a tree reduction in shared memory.
